chunks: Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Bazie ibn Umar ibn Bazie, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was eating vinegar and oil in a black bowl, with the inscription 'Say, He is Allah, One' written in gold in its center. He said to me: 'Approach, O Bazie.' So I approached and ate with him. Then he sipped water three sips when nothing of the bread remained, then he handed it to me, so I sipped the remainder.

key_terms.حَسَا: To sip or gulp down liquid

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) eat and how did he share the meal with his companion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the asceticism (zuhd) and humility of Imam al-Baqir (AS), who shared a simple meal of vinegar and oil with his companion Bazie, emphasizing that spiritual status does not preclude simplicity in daily sustenance. The inscription of Surah Al-Ikhlas on the black bowl serves as a constant reminder of Tawhid during the act of eating, while the practice of sipping water three times reflects the Prophetic tradition of moderation and gratitude. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual mindfulness into mundane acts, such as dining, to cultivate a connection with the Divine.
